## Statistical Analyses - Supplementary

Total RNA. Total RNA was extracted with TRIzol from biopsies taken before the intervention, after 3 weeks (6 sessions) and after the intervention. RNA concentration was measured by NanoDrop spectrophotometry, with four readings per extract. The model was fitted to the individual readings (1,552 observations) rather than to sample means. The outcome was log-transformed and standardised (mean 0, SD 1). Tissue weight (mg) was log-transformed and standardised, so that the relationship between RNA yield and tissue mass was estimated from the data instead of assuming a fixed RNA-per-mg ratio. The estimated log-log slope was [slope from model 4, with 95% CrI].

The model was

ystd ~ mgstd + tx * time + (1 + time | participant) + (1 | participant:leg) + (1 | participant:sample)

where tx has five levels (older low volume, older moderate volume, young low volume, young moderate volume, older control) and time has three (pre, week 3, post). The participant-level intercept and time slope were allowed to correlate. The leg term separates a person’s two legs, and the sample term (sample nested within participant) separates differences between extracts from the technical variation among readings of the same extract.

Priors were Normal(0, 1) on the intercept and on all group and time coefficients, Normal(1, 1) on the mass slope, LKJ(2) on the participant correlation, and Exponential(1) on the three group SDs and the residual SD. Prior predictive simulations were checked before fitting. The model was sampled with four chains, 4,000 iterations, adapt_delta = 0.95 and max_treedepth = 15.

Predictions were computed at the population level (no participant, leg or sample offsets) at the average tissue mass for each group and time point. Contrasts were computed from the posterior draws and back-transformed to ratios with the standard deviation of the log outcome. They were:

change from baseline within each group (pre to week 3, pre to post, and week 3 to post)
the two volume conditions pooled within each age group
moderate vs. low volume within each age group
young vs. older participants in the intervention groups
older intervention vs. control
age difference in the volume effect

Estimates are given as percentage changes or ratios (posterior mean, 95% equal-tailed credible interval).

Protein. UBF and c-Myc were quantified by capillary immunoassay (Jess, ProteinSimple), and peak areas were exported from Compass for Simple Western. The primary outcome was the corrected area, which is the peak area divided by the capillary’s normalisation factor from total-protein normalisation. The factor is scaled to 1 at reference capillary 2 on each plate. c-Myc resolved as two peaks, and the high peak was analysed. The low peak (~48 kDa) was not, because its within-participant SD was about twice that of the high peak (0.91 vs. 0.48 on the log scale) and no model fitted it reliably.

The design had one baseline sample per participant (taken from a randomised leg and assumed equal for both legs) and one week-3 sample from each leg. Sample order within a participant was randomised, and each sample was run once.

The outcome was log-transformed and standardised separately for each protein and analysis. The model was

ystd ~ 0 + tx_sex + tx_sex:time + (1 | participant) + (1 | participant:leg)

where tx_sex is the combination of group and sex. A random participant slope for time was not included, because each participant contributes one baseline and one week-3 sample per leg, so participant-specific change cannot be separated from residual variation. Models with this slope diverged for UBF (up to 85 divergences), and the contrasts agreed within about 3 percentage points with and without it. Priors were Normal(0, 1) on the fixed effects and Exponential(1) on the participant, participant:leg and residual SDs. Sampling used four chains, 10,000 iterations, adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15 and init = 0.1. All models had no divergent transitions, a maximum Rhat ≤ 1.01 and a minimum ESS of 1,588.

Predictions and contrasts were computed from the posterior draws at the population level, with the two sexes weighted equally on the standardised log scale. Draws were back-transformed with each model’s own mean and SD, and contrasts are reported as percentage changes and ratios of changes. Four sensitivity analyses were run:

B: log of the area without normalisation.
C: corrected area with capillaries removed if the normalisation factor was < 0.5 or if Compass issued a warning for the capillary. [For UBF, the factor only; the Compass warnings were not used for exclusion.]
C2 (UBF only): as C with a stricter factor cutoff of 0.4.
D: as the primary model plus a plate intercept (Exponential(1) prior on its SD).

Results are classified as described in the main text. Differences between the sensitivity analyses and the primary analysis are reported only where they change the evidence class.

RNA-seq. Of the [N] samples sequenced, 192 passed quality control and were analysed. Low-abundance genes were removed with edgeR::filterByExpr (minimum count 10, minimum total count 15, large.n 10, minimum proportion 0.7), with sex × age group as the grouping variable. This retained 16,878 genes. Library sizes were normalised with TMM, and the effective library size relative to the median was used as a log offset.

Counts for each gene were modelled with the nbinom2 family in glmmTMB. The linear predictor contained sex, age group (young, 20–30 y; older, > 70 y), a three-level treatment term (baseline, post low volume, post moderate volume), the age × treatment interaction, and a varying intercept for participant. The model was fitted with the seqwrap workflow in two passes.

First pass: an uninformed model was fitted to every gene.
Second pass: a regularised model was fitted using priors built from the first pass.
Fixed effects: Normal priors, with the mean and SD taken across genes from the first-pass estimates of each non-intercept parameter.
Participant SD: a gamma prior with shape set by the mean first-pass estimate and scale fixed at 2.
Dispersion: a Normal prior centred on the value predicted from a loess trend (span 0.7) of first-pass dispersion on log mean raw count, with the residual standard error of the trend as SD.
Intercept: left unpenalised, because its scale differs across genes.

Contrasts were computed on the link scale with marginaleffects::predictions, at the median library size, as linear combinations of the model-predicted group means, averaging the sexes with equal weight. They were:

baseline age difference (young − older)
baseline-to-post change within each age group, averaging the two volume conditions with equal weight
age difference in this change
moderate − low volume, overall and within each age group
age difference in the volume effect

Each contrast was tested with a Wald test. P-values were adjusted with Benjamini–Hochberg separately for each contrast, across all 16,878 genes, and genes with FDR < 5% were regarded as differentially expressed.

Gene-set enrichment used clusterProfiler::gseGO (biological process; set size 25–500; 10,000 permutations; exact p-values with eps = 0). Genes were ranked by the Wald statistic of the contrast, and redundant terms were collapsed with simplify (similarity cutoff 0.5, retaining the term with the largest |NES|). Genes with FDR < 1% that belong to no biological-process gene set were identified. Their residual correlations (from a model of log-CPM values with the same fixed and random effects) were shrunk with corpcor, clustered (Ward’s D2 on 1 − |r|, six clusters), and annotated by gene-set enrichment of each gene’s correlation profile.
